messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INCIDENT #INC-2026-042 — region=us-east, availability_zone=us-east-3, symptom=high pod evictions + autoscaler errors, severity=P1. PD link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/INC-2026-042

pagerduty: Triggered alert. Escalation policy: infra-sre -> eng-l2. See alert runbook: https://runbooks.local/az-outage

sarah (oncall): ack — I'm on it. Noted spike of 503s from hosted API in us-east-3. Time window ~10:18 UTC.

josh: looking at node logs — repeated OOM/kubelet evictions and driver errors on inferencer pool us-east-3 (pool-id: infer-us3-rt). eviction rate ~92% across the pool.

maya: Can we proactively shift traffic off az3? If autoscaler keeps flapping we'll keep impacting customers.

sarah (oncall): I'll start a controlled failover. Plan: 1) canary 5% to other AZs, 2) if stable -> 100%, 3) warm fallback pools in us-east-1 first.

josh: stack snippet from node-az3-12: 
```
kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (inference) score 987
nv_peer_mem: failed to register for ibv_reg_mr
kubelet: eviction manager: memory available below eviction threshold
```

maya: sounds like a host-level regression — maybe last night's host firmware. I'll open vendor ticket but we should cut traffic first.

eng-oncall: Verified autoscaler logs -> repeated "scale_provision_timeout" error between 10:15-10:22 UTC. Suggest preventing new scheduling into az3.

sarah (oncall): executing routing override now — will canary. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.local/route/override \
  -d '{"region":"us-east","avoid":["us-east-3"],"reason":"AZ3 autoscaler churn"}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

incident-bot: Runbook pinned: "AZ outage -> failover". Playbook step 1: set routing override, step 2: warm fallback pool, step 3: customer comms.

josh: opening vendor TAC: NIC vendor ticket TAC-56321 — includes kernel OOPS and nv_peer_mem stack.

maya: creating warm pool in us-east-1 to accept diverted traffic and pre-fill KV caches. Commands: 
```
rctl create-pool --name warm-fallback-us-east-1 --size 12 --model gpt-medium --quant q4_0
rctl wait-pool ready warm-fallback-us-east-1
prefill-cache --pool warm-fallback-us-east-1 --models top20
```

ops-bot: Notified #sre-leads and created dedicated incident channel #inc-1977654321.

pagerduty: Automatic escalation in 3m if not acknowledged by L2.

maya: warm-fallback-us-east-1 pool ready in ~9m, starting cache prefill now.

josh: cordoning az3 nodes to avoid new scheduling while we observe:
```
kubectl cordon node-az3-*
kubectl drain node-az3-* --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data=false
```

sarah (oncall): customer impact initial assessment: approx 8% of total routed requests hit failing hosts in us-east-3 causing 502/503s. Two dedicated customers reported errors to support. Marking severity P1 and contacting account teams.

maya: prefill progress: 100% for top-10 models, 76% for top-20. KV cache warm time ~2m per model.

josh: networking telemetry shows increased retransmits and IB RDMA errors consistent with new firmware. Adding kernel/NIC tags to incident.

sarah (oncall): starting canary shift: 10% -> us-east-{1,2}. Monitoring latency and error budgets.

incident-bot: Traffic override applied: canary 10% away from us-east-3. Monitoring hooks enabled.

maya: 10% canary looks stable (latency + error within SLO). Increasing to 50%.

sarah (oncall): 50% done. Observed small drop in KV hit ratio but p95 latency unchanged. Proceeding to 100% away from us-east-3. Reducing routing TTL to 30s to converge faster.

incident-bot: Traffic override: 100% away from us-east-3 applied. Live traffic is now routed to us-east-1/2.

josh: autoscaler churn in az3 continues but impact on end users mitigated by routing. We'll keep pools cordoned for now.

sarah (oncall): notifying Accounts & Support: draft message: "Hi — we experienced an AZ-level disruption in us-east-3 that caused transient 5xx errors for a subset of requests. We have shifted traffic to healthy AZs and are monitoring. We're investigating the root cause (host firmware/networking) and will update every 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption." Sending now.

ops-bot: Created customer incident tickets: CUST-9823 (reserved), CUST-7741 (hosted).

maya: next steps: schedule maintenance to roll back last-night host firmware in us-east-3 and run validation. I'll coordinate with infra.

josh: adding kernel and NIC telemetry to our dashboards and creating alerts for nv_peer_mem failures to catch regressions during rollback.

sarah (oncall): timeline note for PD: page fired 10:18 UTC, ack 10:19 UTC, failover completed 10:33 UTC. Marking incident status -> mitigated for customer impact; keeping open for RCA.

alan: acknowledged handoff at 13:00 UTC. I'll own monitoring and drive the RCA with infra and vendor TAC.

sarah (oncall): thanks everyone :thumbsup: great coordination. I'll create the postmortem doc and assign action items.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" by sarah (oncall) at 10:33 UTC. Postmortem scheduled: https://pm.local/incidents/1977654321/postmortem

sarah (oncall): leaving the channel to alan for next-phase RCA. If anything flares, please page the infra-sre escalation.

alan: will keep watch and update if vendor provides a fix.

mike (random-observer): :thumbsup: solid playbook execution
